consumer.title: A Connected Livestream-Production Suite
consumer.body: StreamSuites is centered on two production experiences: Browser Studio and the native Windows StudioApp. StreamSuites Studio for OBS extends the same system into existing OBS workflows, while automation, engagement, alerts, public profiles, and creator tools connect around the show.

developer.title: Production Surfaces over Shared Runtime/Auth Authority
developer.body: StreamSuites Studio, StudioApp, and StreamSuites Studio for OBS are separate clients with separate media ownership. The Python Runtime/Auth repository is the sole authority for shared identity, permissions, rooms, invitations, destinations, credentials, automation state, alerts, exports, and canonical project versioning; it is not a shared media engine.

sections.title: A Product Family, Not One Monolith

consumer.title: Purpose-Built Surfaces
consumer.body: Browser production, native Windows production, OBS integration, Creator configuration, Public experiences, administration, developer tools, documentation, and FindMeHere discovery each have a focused surface. They feel connected because they rely on the same authoritative system underneath.

developer.title: Repository and Authority Boundaries
developer.body: StreamSuites is the authoritative Runtime/Auth repository. StreamSuites-Studio, StreamSuites-StudioApp, StreamSuites-OBS, Public, Creator, Dashboard/Admin, Developer, Docs, Members/FindMeHere, and LiveChat Launcher are clients with distinct responsibilities. Authenticated Creator and Admin writes flow through permission-checked Runtime/Auth APIs; no client creates a competing canonical store.

consumer.title: Useful Foundations, Explicit Limits
consumer.body: StreamSuites is in active Alpha development. Meaningful foundations are implemented, but products and modules are at different stages and may still change. Access, availability, and capability labels are kept visible so previews are not mistaken for general availability.

developer.title: Runtime-Authoritative System Version
developer.body: Runtime/Auth owns canonical project version and build metadata. Independently distributed components may publish clearly labelled product release identities without replacing system authority. Alpha contracts may change; each product repository remains authoritative for its narrower validation and availability posture.

consumer.title: One Coordinated Identity and State System
consumer.body: Accounts, permissions, rooms, invitations, destinations, alerts, and shared creator state come from one authority. Public pages and product clients present approved views of that state instead of inventing their own.

developer.title: Canonical APIs, Stores, and Safe Projections
developer.body: Runtime/Auth owns canonical SQLite and protected credential state, authenticated APIs, deterministic public exports, and version metadata. Downstream surfaces consume authorized payloads or public-safe projections. Client-local settings may remain local only when they do not compete with identity, permission, room, destination, credential, or shared-project authority.

consumer.title: Public Results Without Exposing Private State
consumer.body: Clips, polls, tallies, scores, profiles, progression, and live discovery can be shown publicly through deliberately shaped data without exposing private credentials or internal control state.

developer.title: Mirrors and Hydration Inputs, Not Competing Truth
developer.body: Runtime exports are deterministic mirrors and hydration inputs. Public routes may combine existing same-origin public APIs with checked-in or generated fallback exports, but they do not treat a stale mirror as independent authority and never expose session cookies, OAuth tokens, stream keys, provider credentials, or internal-only fields.

consumer.title: Connected Control, Product-Owned Media
consumer.body: The suite coordinates access and state centrally, but video and audio follow the architecture appropriate to each production product.

developer.title: Three Media Boundaries
developer.body: Browser Studio connects directly to Cloudflare RealtimeKit using Runtime/Auth-issued participant credentials. StudioApp keeps local capture, composition, audio, encoding, recording, replay, and direct output in its supervised native C++ engine. StreamSuites Studio for OBS delivers authorized guest tracks to loopback OBS Browser Sources while OBS retains scenes, mixing, encoding, recording, and streaming. None of these media paths terminates in Python.

consumer.title: Predictable Background Work
consumer.body: Long-running jobs, room activity, platform workers, and media supervision are designed to start, report state, and stop cleanly rather than hiding uncontrolled background behavior.

developer.title: Explicit Ownership and Cleanup
developer.body: Runtime schedulers, browser media sessions, StudioApp Engine.Host supervision, and OBS plugin workers each retain explicit ownership, bounded retries, cancellation, redacted diagnostics, and controlled shutdown within their own architecture. A client does not silently duplicate another product's worker or media lifecycle.

consumer.title: Settings Where They Belong
consumer.body: Creators and operators can configure the suite through focused interfaces, while sensitive or shared settings stay protected by the central authority.

developer.title: Server-Backed Shared State and Local Device State
developer.body: Runtime/Auth owns shared configuration, integrations, credentials, destinations, roles, permissions, rooms, and account state. StudioApp may own machine-local device, workspace, hotkey, and path settings. Browser and static clients do not turn localStorage or exported JSON into canonical shared state.

consumer.title: Guardrails Around Shared Capabilities
consumer.body: Permissions, tiers, cooldowns, and usage limits protect shared services and keep actions scoped to the right creator and room.

developer.title: Runtime-Owned Enforcement
developer.body: Roles and tiers remain distinct. Runtime/Auth performs permission checks, creator scoping, destination ownership checks, cooldown policy, quota tracking, access grants, and session enforcement. Public presentation can explain or render those states but cannot weaken or replace server enforcement.

consumer.title: Rules That Support the Show
consumer.body: Chat events, triggers, and automation remain part of StreamSuites, but they now support a production-centered product family rather than standing alone as the whole identity.

developer.title: Mixed-Maturity, Runtime-Owned Automation
developer.body: Provider-aware event normalization, creator-scoped trigger registries, cooldown policy, controlled actions, and operator surfaces exist at mixed maturity. Action execution and cross-platform coverage are not uniformly complete. Runtime/Auth retains execution and policy authority; product clients consume capability and state contracts.

consumer.title: Engagement Around the Production
consumer.body: Clips, polls, tallies, scoreboards, wheels, games, profiles, progression, alerts, and overlays remain connected suite capabilities for creators and audiences.

developer.title: Runtime Contracts at Different Maturity Levels
developer.body: Runtime-owned schemas, stores, APIs, and exports exist across engagement modules at different maturity levels. Public, Creator, and Admin surfaces consume those contracts without inventing missing backend fields or presenting every module as a complete live workflow.

consumer.title: Different Pipelines for Different Jobs
consumer.body: Public clips and native local production media can both appear in the suite, but they come from separate workflows with separate ownership.

developer.title: Runtime Clips and StudioApp Local Media Are Separate
developer.body: The Runtime clipping module publishes public-safe artifacts through its own bounded pipeline. StudioApp's native recording, replay, and Clip workflow stays inside its C++ media engine and local storage contract. Browser Studio recording and broadcast output remain unimplemented.

consumer.title: Public Pages Resolve Real Published State
consumer.body: Public galleries, profiles, and discovery views load authorized published data and keep clear loading, empty, degraded, and unavailable states when that data cannot be resolved.

developer.title: API-First and Export-Fallback Resolution
developer.body: Public features preserve their established API, query, hash, slug, and fallback resolution contracts. Runtime-generated copies remain mirrors. Version and status widgets hydrate their existing endpoints, and route aliases or Cloudflare redirects remain part of the deployed contract.

sections.title: Focused Public, Creator, and Admin Experiences

consumer.title: The Right Surface for Each Audience
consumer.body: Public presents profiles and published artifacts, Creator manages creator-facing settings and integrations, and Admin provides privileged operational workflows.

developer.title: Clients of Runtime/Auth, Not Standalone Authorities
developer.body: Public is a read-oriented public and authenticated-account client. Creator and Dashboard/Admin may perform implemented permission-checked writes through Runtime/Auth. Developer, Docs, Members/FindMeHere, and LiveChat Launcher remain focused clients. Their local presentation state never displaces authoritative account, role, tier, room, integration, or shared-project state.
